questions.questionText:
Out of the four given figures A, B, C, and D, three are similar in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd figure out:

Figures A, B, and C are closed polygons (Triangle, Rectangle, Pentagon), whereas Figure D is an open spiral curve.
questions.hint: Check structural properties: closed vs open, number of sides (odd/even), symmetry, or rotational sense.
questions.explanation: Figures A, B, and C are closed geometric polygons composed of straight line segments, whereas Figure D is an open non-closed curve.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Check basic properties: number of straight lines, closed vs open contours.
Step 2: Check symmetry and rotational direction.
Step 3: The odd figure that does not conform to the group rule is Figure D (open curve).
questions.memoryTip: Odd Figure Out Checklist: 1. Closed/Open, 2. Side count, 3. Symmetry, 4. Shading ratio, 5. Direction of rotation.

questions.questionText:

solutionSteps: Step 1: Check basic properties: number of straight lines, closed vs open contours.
Step 2: Check symmetry and rotational direction.
Step 3: The odd figure that does not conform to the group rule is Figure D (asymmetrical figure).

Figures A, B, and C are closed polygons (Triangle, Rectangle, Pentagon), whereas Figure D is an open spiral curve.
questions.hint: Check structural properties: closed vs open, number of sides (odd/even), symmetry, or rotational sense.
questions.explanation: Figures A, B, and C are closed geometric polygons composed of straight line segments, whereas Figure D is an open non-closed curve.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Check basic properties: number of straight lines, closed vs open contours.
Step 2: Check symmetry and rotational direction.
Step 3: The odd figure that does not conform to the group rule is Figure D (open curve).
questions.memoryTip: Odd Figure Out Checklist: 1. Closed/Open, 2. Side count, 3. Symmetry, 4. Shading ratio, 5. Direction of rotation.

questions.questionText:

solutionSteps: Step 1: Check basic properties: number of straight lines, closed vs open contours.
Step 2: Check symmetry and rotational direction.
Step 3: The odd figure that does not conform to the group rule is Figure D (asymmetrical figure).

Figures A, B, and C are closed polygons (Triangle, Rectangle, Pentagon), whereas Figure D is an open spiral curve.
questions.hint: Check structural properties: closed vs open, number of sides (odd/even), symmetry, or rotational sense.
questions.explanation: Figures A, B, and C are closed geometric polygons composed of straight line segments, whereas Figure D is an open non-closed curve.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Check basic properties: number of straight lines, closed vs open contours.
Step 2: Check symmetry and rotational direction.
Step 3: The odd figure that does not conform to the group rule is Figure D (open curve).
questions.memoryTip: Odd Figure Out Checklist: 1. Closed/Open, 2. Side count, 3. Symmetry, 4. Shading ratio, 5. Direction of rotation.

questions.questionText:

solutionSteps: Step 1: Check basic properties: number of straight lines, closed vs open contours.
Step 2: Check symmetry and rotational direction.
Step 3: The odd figure that does not conform to the group rule is Figure D (asymmetrical figure).

Figures A, B, and C are closed polygons (Triangle, Rectangle, Pentagon), whereas Figure D is an open spiral curve.
questions.hint: Check structural properties: closed vs open, number of sides (odd/even), symmetry, or rotational sense.
questions.explanation: Figures A, B, and C are closed geometric polygons composed of straight line segments, whereas Figure D is an open non-closed curve.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Check basic properties: number of straight lines, closed vs open contours.
Step 2: Check symmetry and rotational direction.
Step 3: The odd figure that does not conform to the group rule is Figure D (open curve).
questions.memoryTip: Odd Figure Out Checklist: 1. Closed/Open, 2. Side count, 3. Symmetry, 4. Shading ratio, 5. Direction of rotation.

questions.questionText:

solutionSteps: Step 1: Check basic properties: number of straight lines, closed vs open contours.
Step 2: Check symmetry and rotational direction.
Step 3: The odd figure that does not conform to the group rule is Figure D (asymmetrical figure).

Figures A, B, and C are closed polygons (Triangle, Rectangle, Pentagon), whereas Figure D is an open spiral curve.
questions.hint: Check structural properties: closed vs open, number of sides (odd/even), symmetry, or rotational sense.
questions.explanation: Figures A, B, and C are closed geometric polygons composed of straight line segments, whereas Figure D is an open non-closed curve.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Check basic properties: number of straight lines, closed vs open contours.
Step 2: Check symmetry and rotational direction.
Step 3: The odd figure that does not conform to the group rule is Figure D (open curve).
questions.memoryTip: Odd Figure Out Checklist: 1. Closed/Open, 2. Side count, 3. Symmetry, 4. Shading ratio, 5. Direction of rotation.

questions.questionText:

solutionSteps: Step 1: Check basic properties: number of straight lines, closed vs open contours.
Step 2: Check symmetry and rotational direction.
Step 3: The odd figure that does not conform to the group rule is Figure D (asymmetrical figure).
